summary:
Session Summary
---------------

The party spent the session planning their next moves against the lich while pursuing leads involving Grixto, Galixtar, and the Dragon Rider training grounds in The Reach. Walker departed through the gate with Elrus, Araden, Glimmen, and eventually Plymouth Gawater to conduct a scouting mission, investigate the training grounds, recharge his gems, and uncover information about the lich and the keystones, while the remaining party traveled toward Langdale and left two keystones with Juten Prime for safekeeping. The group discussed the lich’s possible phylactery, suspecting his recurring chess-like pieces might provide a clue, and learned more about Al Kurin vessels and Grixto’s activities. Meanwhile, Gerk experimented with his new Doorman ability, opening portals to strange environments and eventually attempting to reach Mahali’s home from the moving ship. The doorway caused severe spatial distortion, stretching the ship and surrounding reality until the party reversed course. Closing the doorway triggered a powerful magical discharge: Gerk became confused, everyone aboard became unable to see or normally hear one another, spellcasters regained expended spell slots, and a giant spectral door and golden magical track appeared. The party discovered that physical contact and vibrations could still cross the strange separation and improvised ways to locate one another, including coins, olive oil, and a summoned constrictor snake. The session ended with the party attempting to understand the spectral door, Gerk’s condition, and the consequences of the magical event while Walker’s expedition continued in The Reach.

plotSections.title: Planning the Next Destination
bullets: The party's immediate goal is to track down the lich and investigate leads connected to Grixto and Galixtar. They consider returning to Langdale for information, investigating the lich's former hideout in The Reach, and eventually visiting the Dragon Rider training grounds.

The Reach is accessible by the party's boat, by a captain who regularly travels between realms, or through the gatehouse using its keystones. Walker's Gate spell cannot transport the boat because its maximum diameter is 20 feet.
The party has sufficient food and water aboard the boat and can potentially resupply at a centrally located port city in The Reach.

plotSections.title: The Party's Crew and Elrus
bullets: The party confirms that their four surviving-and-revived crew members are Abel, Garrett, Bill, and Fritz. Abel is the helmsman and Garrett is the gunner; the exact roles of Bill and Fritz remain unclear, although one is believed to be a greenhorn.
Walker has an obligation to take Elrus somewhere because he previously promised the very old man a place to stay. Walker plans to bring Elrus with him when investigating The Reach.

plotSections.title: Grixto, Galixtar, and the Dragon Rider Training Grounds
bullets: The party has a lead suggesting Grixto and Galixtar were near caves associated with the Dragon Rider training grounds. Walker's previous vision prompted interest in investigating the area.

The caves and Walker's former roost in The Reach are believed to have been uninhabited for a long time, making it uncertain whether Grixto remains there. Walker nevertheless wants to exhaust the lead.

The training grounds are roughly a couple of days' flight from Walker's former residence in The Reach. From the area near the Whispering Abyss, the training grounds are approximately five days of flight away, near the Lost Isles and mountains between three islands.

Sylan prefers any investigation to remain a scouting mission so that a confrontation with Grixto occurs only when the entire party can respond. Walker considers traveling with Elrus and Araden, although he recognizes the danger of encountering Grixto.
Walker also wants to visit The Reach to recharge his gems.

plotSections.title: Al Kurin
bullets: Grixto had been collecting Al Kurin from other trainees at the Dragon Rider training grounds, including juvenile dragons.
An Al Kurin is a vessel capable of containing and transporting a dragon's soul, so the collected vessels do not necessarily have to remain at the training grounds.
The proximity of the training grounds to Walker's former residence makes it difficult to explain how Grixto could have remained there unnoticed for an extended period.

plotSections.title: The Lich and Its Phylactery
bullets: The party has learned more about the lich but remains uncertain about his current location and the identity of his phylactery.

The party believes the phylactery is a mundane object that the lich keeps on his person. His repeated association with small chess-like or war-game pieces leads Sylan to speculate that a chess set or one of its pieces could be the phylactery.
The party's lore establishes that a phylactery is a vessel containing a lich's soul, although they do not know the precise mechanics by which the lich returns after bodily destruction.

plotSections.title: Walker's Scouting Expedition
bullets: Walker plans to travel to The Reach with Elrus and Araden to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds and search for information about Grixto and Galixtar.
The group intends to remain small and mobile and to retreat immediately if they encounter serious danger rather than initiating a confrontation.

Walker takes the party's sending stone so he can communicate with the others once per day using a message of up to 25 words. The party is uncertain how its recharge interacts with The Reach's unusual flow of time.

Walker initially intends to retain his keystone during the expedition despite Sylan suggesting that he leave it with the party for safety. The party also worries that storing multiple keystones together in a Bag of Holding could create an especially valuable target.

Plymouth Gawater ultimately joins Walker, Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen after consulting Juten Prime. Plymouth's investigation is intended to uncover information about the Dragon Riders, the keystones, and Grixto and Galixtar.

plotSections.title: Time Between Realms
bullets: The party estimates that traveling from their current location to Langdale takes roughly five to seven days by boat.

Time flows differently in The Reach, with the party discussing an approximate ratio of one day in their current realm to seven days in The Reach. Walker can therefore spend considerably longer in The Reach while only a relatively short period passes for the rest of the party.
The party plans to travel toward Langdale while Walker's group conducts its investigation and expects the unusual time difference to affect when they reconnect.

plotSections.title: Keystone and Gatehouse Mechanics
bullets: Plymouth explains that keystones must be properly seated and calibrated by the gatehouse's Doorman before a gate can be safely activated. Gerk, as the current Doorman, is responsible for helping orient and calibrate the stones.

A keystone used to open a gate must remain at the originating gatehouse while the gate is open. It can only be removed after the gate is closed, and tampering with a keystone during activation can cause dangerous malfunctions, as demonstrated by the earlier Gilbrick incident.
The gate functions as a connection between locations rather than allowing the keystone itself to travel through the gate.
Walker immediately activates the Reach gate despite Plymouth's explanation and travels through it with Glimmen, Elrus, and Araden. Plymouth then joins the expedition.

With Plymouth gone, the remaining party will rely on Gerk to operate the keystones and gates. Juten Prime safeguards the two unclaimed keystones while the party takes responsibility for the keystones they have claimed.

plotSections.title: The Ruined Archives and Keystone Research
bullets: The mountain's former libraries and archives are largely destroyed. Evidence suggests both deliberate raiding and natural deterioration, with paper materials mostly gone and stone, slate, and tile records broken or removed.
Only roughly the upper third of the mountain has been explored, leaving substantial portions of the site unexamined.
Sylan theorizes that information in the surviving archives may explain how Grixto learned to use the keystones.
Dana finds little immediately useful research remaining but wants to discuss Plymouth's discoveries about the gatehouse and its history when he returns.
Juten Prime agrees to safeguard the two remaining keystones and continue investigating the site while Plymouth pursues the Dragon Rider lead.

plotSections.title: Gerk Experiments with the Doorman Ability
bullets: After Walker's departure, Gerk begins experimenting with his new Doorman ability, which allows him to open door-like portals by concentrating on destinations.

His first experiments open onto radically different environments, including a murky body of water that sends swamp-smelling water through the opening and a barren, rocky landscape with geysers, intense heat, steam, and sulfurous air.
The portals manifest as tangible-looking doors that are actually openings or reflections of another location. Opening or closing one takes an action in combat.
Gerk and Sylan plan to continue practicing the ability during the voyage, initially attempting to reach familiar locations such as Gerk's home.

plotSections.title: The Moving Ship Doorway
bullets: Gerk attempts to open a door to his house while standing at the rear of the moving ship. Sylan uses Beacon of Hope to assist with the required Wisdom saving throws, and both avoid losing sanity.

The open doorway causes the ship and surrounding reality to stretch in a rubber-band-like distortion while the doorway remains fixed in place. The ship itself continues moving rather than physically slowing down.
The doorway exerts a powerful pull on Gerk. He makes a Strength saving throw and rolls 31, allowing him to hold onto it despite the force.

Mahali appears through the doorway from his kitchen and pulls Gerk through to safety. Passing through the doorway feels like moving through thick smoke or water, and the doorway remains open after Gerk passes through.

When the ship reverses course, the distortion reverses with it and eventually brings the ship back into alignment with the doorway. The incident demonstrates that using the ability from a moving vessel can dangerously distort space and reality.

plotSections.title: Closing the Door
bullets: The party decides to close the unstable doorway after preparing ropes and other precautions and evacuating Mahali's stronghold as a safety measure.

Gerk steps through the doorway and experiences another temporal or dimensional transition before closing it. The closure produces a quiet snap, followed by blinding light tracing the stretched path between the ship's previous and current positions.
Gerk rolls a 5 on a d10 for the door's effect. The DM describes the result as roughly midway on the relevant chart and pauses to determine the unexpected consequences.
The party braces for the possibility of being displaced or otherwise harmed, with Dana prepared to use Feather Fall if necessary.

plotSections.title: The Magical Discharge
bullets: Closing Gerk's doorway triggers a powerful magical discharge that causes reality around the ship to snap back into cohesion.
Gerk fails a Wisdom save and becomes confused and unable to act normally, while Sylan succeeds and remains functional.
Everyone aboard appears to blink out of existence or become invisible to the others. The party can still physically interact, but normal sight and sound between individuals are disrupted.

Dana and Sylan recognize the magical sensation as similar to what they experienced in the presence of deities and realize that their spells have become greatly empowered. All expended spell slots are restored.
A giant, closed, shining spectral door appears near where Gerk had been standing. Its appearance strongly resembles Gerk's door when his shield is in door form.
A thin golden, semi-fluorescent line remains embedded through the ship along the path of the magical discharge, resembling a lightning strike without causing physical damage.

plotSections.title: The Party's Separation
bullets: The party remains unable to see one another, recalling a similar separation that occurred in La-rel. Normal sounds do not reliably travel between the separated individuals.

Physical interaction remains possible despite the invisibility. Ciri can make contact with Sylan, Sylan can touch Gerk, and vibrations through the ship can be detected even when the associated sounds cannot.
Gerk remains confused and largely unable to communicate, making him especially difficult to locate and assist.

plotSections.title: The Spectral Door and Gerk
bullets: The spectral door continues hovering near Gerk, who is invisible and unable to move normally.
Sylan discovers Gerk by physically walking into him and attempts to support and reposition him. Gerk eventually allows himself to fall, and Sylan catches and lowers him.
Sylan turns Gerk toward the spectral door and attempts to determine whether the door or the forces around it are responsible for Gerk's condition.

plotSections.title: Attempts to Communicate and Restore Visibility
bullets: Sylan uses coins arranged on the deck to create visible messages for the unseen party members, eventually indicating Gerk's name and location.
Ord considers using powder or dust to reveal invisible people but instead uses his dragon vessel to pour olive oil over himself.
The oil experiment partially succeeds: although Ord remains invisible, the oil forms a faint, visible, largely silent silhouette outlining the portions of his body it covers.

Dana summons a large constrictor snake from her serpentine bracers and keeps it near her heel, giving her another visible marker for tracking her position. The DM establishes that the command can produce two constrictor snakes, though whether they can be released individually remains unresolved.

plotSections.title: The Reach
bullets: While the party deals with the magical aftermath, Walker describes The Reach as being in autumn, with crisp weather around 60 degrees and changing fall colors.

The Reach has a flying-themed culture, including the National Flying League, a flying sport jokingly compared to Quidditch, floating jack-o'-lanterns, and seasonal apple cider sold by a familiar turtle-like vendor.
